section_summary: This section covers State Department records relating to the erection, dedication, and custody of monuments and memorials in Japan honoring prominent Americans. Primary subjects include monuments to Townsend Harris at Jigan-in temple in Kawazu and Zempukuji temple in Tokyo, the deposit of Harris and Commodore Perry relics at Ryosenji temple in Shimoda, and a memorial to Thomas Alva Edison at Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine in Yawata. Additional items reference monuments to anthropologist Frederick Starr in Tokyo and General Ulysses S. Grant in Ueno Park.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting a report on the Japanese legend of Townsend Harris and Okichi.
subfiles.summary: A Document File Note recording Tokyo Despatch No. 245 (filed under 894.00 P.R./33) dated September 5, 1930. It concerns the widespread popularity in Japan of the legend of Townsend Harris and Okichi. It notes that a new shrine in Tokyo will enshrine a wooden figure of Fudo-son named 'Black Ships Okichi Fudo-son.'
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.413/17 regarding Townsend Harris and Okichi Legend

subfiles.about: Report on the popular legend of Townsend Harris and Okichi in Japanese theater, cinema, songs, and religious shrines.
subfiles.summary: An excerpt from a periodic report discussing the growing popularity of the legendary romance between Townsend Harris and his maid Okichi. It describes popular recordings, plays, and the silent film 'Tojin Okichi,' providing translations of two theme songs about the 'Black Ships.' It also details the establishment of a shrine in Nihonbashi, Tokyo, housing a statue of Fudo-son associated with treaty negotiator Shimejiro Isa.
subfiles.title: Report on Conditions in Japan: Popularity of the Townsend Harris and Okichi Legend

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum suggesting Foreign Service Journal publication of Despatch No. 433.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum noting Tokyo Despatch No. 433 regarding Ambassador Grew's inscription for a monument at a temple where Townsend Harris stayed in 1857. It suggests that the Foreign Service Journal might make use of the despatch.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Despatch No. 433

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting Ambassador Grew's dedicatory inscription for a monument to Townsend Harris at Jigan-in temple.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports complying with a request from the abbot of Jigan-in temple in Kawazu to provide an inscription for a monument marking Townsend Harris's overnight stay in 1857. With the assistance of Midori Komatsu, an inscription and photograph of Grew were provided to the temple. The despatch transmits a translation of a formal letter of gratitude signed by the abbot, local officials, and temple supporters.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 433: Inscription Written by Ambassador Grew to Commemorate Visit of Townsend Harris to a Temple Near Shimoda

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum summarizing the settlement of the custody dispute over Townsend Harris relics at Shimoda.
subfiles.summary: A memorandum reviewing Tokyo Despatch No. 602 regarding the resolution of a dispute between Shimoda town authorities and the priest of Ryosenji temple. It notes that a contract was signed placing donated relics in the custody of the priest to be exhibited in the temple's Memorial Hall.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Despatch No. 602

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the delivery of Townsend Harris and Commodore Perry relics to Ryosenji temple in Shimoda.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew explains that relics contributed by Helen Harris Vreeland, Professor M. E. Cosenza, and the U.S. Navy Department had been held at the Embassy pending the completion of a Memorial Hall and resolution of municipal disputes in Shimoda. A contract was concluded between Mayor Toranosuke Suzuki and Chief Priest Kiichi Shimizu to house the relics in the Busankaku building at Ryosenji. Enclosures include the contract, a detailed relic inventory, and correspondence with Mrs. Vreeland.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 602: Presentation of Townsend Harris Relics to the Ryosen Temple at Shimoda

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting the unveiling of a monument to Thomas Alva Edison in Japan.
subfiles.summary: A Document File Note recording Kobe Despatch No. 323 (filed under 894.415-Edison/1) dated May 28, 1934. It notes the erection and unveiling of a monument to Thomas Alva Edison on May 23, 1934.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.413/20 regarding Edison Monument

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording a report on the monument unveiled in memory of Dr. Frederick Starr.
subfiles.summary: A Document File Note referencing Despatch No. 917 (Periodic Report No. 80) of August 4, 1934. It records the unveiling of a monument in Tokyo in memory of the late Dr. Frederick Starr.
subfiles.title: Document File Note 894.413/21 regarding Frederick Starr Monument

subfiles.about: Report extract describing the unveiling of a stone monument to American anthropologist Dr. Frederick Starr in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: An excerpt from Periodic Report No. 80 reporting that a stone monument was unveiled in Tokyo on July 6, 1934, honoring Dr. Frederick Starr. The ceremony was organized by the Bosatsu-kai society to recognize Starr's contributions to Japanese-American cultural relations. The page also mentions planned journalist exchanges and a student conference.
subfiles.title: Extract from Periodic Report No. 80: Monument Unveiled in Memory of the Late Frederick Starr

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the unveiling of a monument to Townsend Harris at Zempukuji temple in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports on the unveiling of a black stone and bronze monument dedicated to Townsend Harris at Zempukuji, the site of the first American Legation in Tokyo. The monument was unveiled by Mrs. Grew and sponsored by the America-Japan Society with key backing from Takashi Masuda. The despatch includes Grew's speech text and press clippings from The Japan Times and The Japan Advertiser containing addresses by Prince Tokugawa and Masuda.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2195: Unveiling of Townsend Harris Monument

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum suggesting that a memorial pamphlet be sent to Professor M. E. Cosenza.
subfiles.summary: A brief internal note suggesting that a copy of the Townsend Harris memorial dedication pamphlet be sent to Professor M. E. Cosenza of the College of the City of New York. It highlights Cosenza's expertise on Townsend Harris and his past assistance to the Embassy in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Townsend Harris Pamphlet

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting commemorative booklets describing the Townsend Harris memorial dedication at Zempukuji.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew transmits five copies of a booklet titled 'The Townsend Harris Memorial: Addresses at the Dedication.' The booklet contains an English foreword by Yasunosuke Fukukita, historical photographs of Zempukuji and the ceremony, and the full speeches delivered by Prince Iyesato Tokugawa, Ambassador Grew, and Takashi Masuda commemorating the 1859 founding of the first U.S. Legation.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 2488: The Townsend Harris Memorial

subfiles.about: Photographs documenting the Townsend Harris monument unveiling ceremony at Zempukuji.
subfiles.summary: Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 2195, consisting of mount cards and inscriptions for four photographs taken during the December 19, 1936 dedication ceremony at Zempukuji. The views depict Ambassador Grew and Takashi Masuda, Prince Tokugawa speaking, Ambassador Grew speaking, and Mrs. Grew unveiling the tablet.
subfiles.title: Photographs of Townsend Harris Monument Dedication (Enclosure No. 3 to Despatch No. 2195)

subfiles.about: Letter from the U.S. Military Academy acknowledging receipt of the Townsend Harris memorial booklet.
subfiles.from: Donald F. Booth, West Point, New York
subfiles.summary: Captain Donald F. Booth, Assistant Adjutant at West Point, writes to Stanley K. Hornbeck to express thanks on behalf of the Acting Superintendent for the Townsend Harris memorial pamphlet. He confirms that the publication has been placed in the Military Academy Library.
subfiles.title: Letter from U.S. Military Academy Acknowledging Harris Memorial Pamphlet
subfiles.to: Stanley K. Hornbeck, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

subfiles.about: Subject file jacket for State Department records relating to the Edison memorial in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The archival document jacket for file 894.413-EDISON, regarding the erection of a monument to Thomas Alva Edison in Japan.
subfiles.title: Subject File Jacket 894.413-EDISON

subfiles.about: Despatch reporting the unveiling of a monument to Thomas Alva Edison at Iwashimizu Shrine in Yawata.
subfiles.summary: Consul Donovan reports the unveiling on May 23, 1934, of a monument to Thomas Alva Edison at Iwashimizu Hachiman Shrine in Yawata, Kyoto Prefecture. The location was chosen because bamboo from the vicinity provided the filament for Edison's successful incandescent electric lamp. Enclosures include photographs, press clippings from the Osaka Mainichi, and Ambassador Grew's address read by Donovan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 323: Monument Erected in Memory of Thomas A. Edison

subfiles.about: Internal routing slip concerning Kobe Despatch No. 323 on the Edison monument.
subfiles.summary: An internal Department of State routing slip from the Division of Far Eastern Affairs drawing the attention of senior officials to Consul Donovan's despatch on the Edison monument.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Routing Slip on Despatch No. 323
subfiles.to: Assistant Secretary / Under Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Press release describing the unveiling of the Edison memorial monument in Japan and quoting Ambassador Grew.
subfiles.summary: A State Department press release detailing the May 23 dedication of the Edison monument at Iwashimizu Shrine in Yawata. It explains the historical role of local bamboo in Edison's development of the incandescent light bulb and quotes Ambassador Grew's message praising Edison and celebrating Japanese-American friendship.
subfiles.title: Department of State Press Release on the Thomas Alva Edison Monument in Japan

subfiles.about: Letter requesting a copy of the official consular report on the Edison monument dedication.
subfiles.summary: The International Edison Foundation requests a copy or résumé of Consul Howard Donovan's report on the unveiling of the Edison memorial in Kyoto, having noted newspaper reports of the event.
subfiles.title: Letter from International Edison Foundation Requesting Report on Edison Monument
subfiles.to: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State

subfiles.about: Letter transmitting the State Department press release on the Edison monument to the International Edison Foundation.
subfiles.from: Maxwell M. Hamilton, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: The Department of State replies to the International Edison Foundation, enclosing a copy of the July 10 press release concerning the Edison memorial dedication at Yawata and noting that Consul Donovan will transmit particulars directly to Charles Edison.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to International Edison Foundation

subfiles.about: Subject file jacket for records concerning the General Grant monument in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The archival folder jacket for records relating to the monument erected in Ueno Park, Tokyo, in memory of General Ulysses S. Grant.
subfiles.title: Subject File Jacket: General Grant Monument at Ueno Park, Tokyo

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting programs, a pamphlet, and postcards relating to the General Grant monument dedication.
subfiles.summary: Chargé d'Affaires Edwin L. Neville refers to his previous despatch concerning the May 30, 1930 unveiling of the General Ulysses S. Grant monument in Ueno Park, Tokyo. He transmits commemorative exercise programs, a pamphlet, and picture postcards showing the monument and memorial trees planted by General and Mrs. Grant.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 152: Unveiling of Monument to General Grant at Ueno Park, Tokyo
